analysis: Recency-weighted positive sampling did not improve validation: macro HR@10 was 0.5700 versus the prior 0.5713. Electronics declined from 0.370 to 0.350. Current category HR@10 scores were Movies_and_TV 0.615, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.610, Electronics 0.350, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.705. This trial provides no evidence that matching positive sampling to the inference profile’s ten-interaction half-life helps; it does not establish why performance declined. Deterministic sampling checks passed and execution succeeded. Retain uniform positive-position sampling as the stronger observed reference.
code_summary: Per-category LightGCN uses 64-dimensional embeddings and averages the initial embeddings with two graph propagation layers. Scores combine learned user vectors, a 0.5-weighted recency history profile, item vectors, and learned item biases. Training removes every occurrence of the positive item from its history profile and uses uniformly averaged sampled-softmax loss with 32 uniform unseen negatives sampled with replacement. This trial changed only positive-position sampling to a precomputed float64 recency CDF with a ten-interaction half-life, plus deterministic checks using an independent RNG. Architecture, optimizer, regularization, checkpoint selection, predictor writer, four-category routing, and epoch default of 200 remained unchanged.
